{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZdR8VA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDEdhY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 45, "title": "Correct V9938 reverse-Y command termination and LINE completion coordinates", "body": "## Problem

The V9938 command engine wraps reverse-Y block operations above row zero instead of terminating. `crates/msx-core/src/vdp_command.rs:134–169` checks horizontal boundaries and masks negative Y values to ten bits, allowing unintended reads/writes in wrapped VRAM. LINE also lacks reverse-top termination, and `finish_command` excludes its DY update.

These defects can corrupt off-screen data and give subsequent commands stale coordinates. They affect shared MSX2 drawing/copy functionality; no particular commercial-game failure was observed.

## Expected outcome

Terminate reverse-Y operations after processing row zero for every relevant source/destination. Preserve forward-Y wrapping, including mode-dependent physical VRAM aliasing. Store correct completion coordinates and remaining row counts, including LINE's major-axis-dependent endpoint behavior.

Deliver the smallest complete command-engine correction, with necessary integration, fixtures and documentation. Exact arbitration, command-speed modeling and live color writes remain separate work.

## Context

- Baseline: `429c2ec25502e133293c0b581f04adccb0c6f7a1`; clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. Open Issues/PRs are empty. Earlier [Issue #35](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/35) addressed VRAM interleaving; [PR #44](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/44) addressed CPU access ordering.
- Relevant implementation: `crates/msx-core/src/vdp_command.rs`, VDP register/port handling in `vdp.rs`, and Machine scheduling in `lib.rs`. Existing native coverage in `crates/msx-core/tests/msx2.rs` tests ordinary LINE drawing, transfers, forward wrapping and interleaving, but lacks reverse-top and LINE completion-state assertions.
- The [Yamaha V9938 manual](https://www.dinoboards.com.au/assets/video-v9958/yamaha_v9938.pdf), printed pages 76–77 and 85, defines LINE and command completion-register changes. The page-85 table marks LINE DY as changed while DX/NX/NY remain unchanged. Text was inspected; its screenshot was unavailable.
- The [pinned openMSX command engine](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/video/VDPCmdEngine.cc), `clipNY_1`, `clipNY_2` and `executeLine`, supplies precise top-edge and endpoint ordering, with real-hardware confirmation comments. This is upstream behavioral evidence, not a physical measurement performed here. Author implementation and fixtures independently.
- Inspected [existing CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40000956420) report 165 Rust and 98 browser passes, including existing command tests. Those passes do not cover these gaps. No builds or tests were run during this investigation; commercial compatibility remains unestablished.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Correct reverse-Y termination for LMMV, LMMM, LMCM, LMMC, HMMV, HMMM, YMMM and HMMC. Destination-only operations stop at DY=0; LMCM stops at SY=0; copies stop when either relevant coordinate crosses above zero. Include row zero exactly once and perform no wrapped access afterward. Preserve horizontal clipping, byte alignment, overlap order and NY=0 meaning 1024 rows.
- [ ] Update completion state consistently with processed rows. For reverse LMMV starting DY=0, NY=3, process one row, leave encoded DY=1023 and NY=2. For reverse LMMM with SY=0, DY=2, NY=3, process one row and leave SY=1023, DY=1, NY=2. Verify unaffected command registers remain unchanged.
- [ ] Correct LINE top-edge termination and DY writeback. Respect X-major completion testing before a final minor-axis Y advance, and Y-major Y advancement before completion testing. Cover both directions, both major axes, horizontal/vertical/sloped lines, zero-length lines and horizontal-edge termination. Include a Y-major vertical line from DY=10 with major length 3: four pixels are drawn and final DY is 14 downward or 6 upward. Keep DX/NX/NY unchanged. Make any minimal stepping adjustments necessary for correct results.
- [ ] Add independently calculated native regressions across SCREEN 5–8 for every affected command family. Include source-first/destination-first copy clipping, starts at Y=0 and Y=1, exact-height and excessive-height requests, zero NY, forward wrapping and SCREEN 7/8 physical aliasing. Check exact pixels/bytes, completion registers, sentinel preservation and bounded completion. Record meaningful failures against the unchanged baseline and passes after correction.
- [ ] Exercise clipped LMCM/LMMC/HMMC with deliberate transfer stalls and final transfers: no extra data requests, wrapped reads/writes or stuck CE. Retain existing STOP, restart, logical-operation, absent-expansion and CE/TR regressions without requiring an unrelated handshake-timing redesign.
- [ ] Add original CPU-executed port probes for reverse-top termination and a chained command that reuses LINE's completed DY without rewriting it. Assert observable VRAM results. Extend compiled-Wasm browser coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/` to check these results through Canvas pixels, retaining existing reset and video coverage.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 firmware/slots, PSG/SCC audio, disk, SRAM persistence, Wasm/browser lifecycle and ownership/provenance safeguards. Use independently authored fixtures and existing lawful assets; proprietary ROM acquisition and human gameplay are unnecessary. Update affected accuracy documentation and disclose remaining timing and physical-validation uncertainty.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using README dependency setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review under `docs/review-guidelines.md`; resolve blocking findings and accurately distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Compare original edge/LINE probes against the pinned upstream configuration or already available hardware evidence before merge. Record configuration and actual observations if performed. No comparison or physical execution was performed here, and neither is a merge prerequisite.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
